title: Settings deep-merge regression — partial PUT must not wipe omitted top-level or nested-sibling keys
_comment: Seed [S04/C3/R3] settings-merge regression (WP-F06, SUMMARY.md C3/R3, ticket Spike-Corrections). Spike S04 verified that a bare Document::save(['settings'=>$patch]) REPLACES _elementor_page_settings wholesale (top + nested) and PUT {} DELETES the meta — only Document::update_settings($patch) deep-merges (array_replace_recursive). The runner: (1) seeds `merge_regression.seed` (≥3 settings of different types incl. the nested `padding` map AND a 2-row `links` repeater); (2) applies `merge_regression.patch` updating exactly ONE top-level key (background_color) and ONE nested sub-key (padding.top), omitting the rest; (3) asserts `survives` (background_background, the OMITTED nested sibling padding.left, AND both repeater rows) are UNCHANGED and `updates` (background_color, padding.top) took effect. This FAILS if the controller bare-saves instead of update_settings()ing. The test MUST wp_set_current_user(admin) first or save()/update_settings() no-op via is_editable_by_current_user() (C3). The `links` repeater documents the array_replace_recursive shorter-list caveat: patch must NOT touch repeaters or trailing rows go stale.
